title: Ex vivo two-photon imaging of whole-mount skeletal muscles to visualize stem cell behavior
protocol: Anesthetize Pax7EGFP mice with isoflurane in an anesthesia induction chamber.
Transfer the mouse to a flat surface and position the nose cone around the snout and mouth of the mouse to keep it anesthetized.
Shave the hair off the hindlimb with an Electric Razor.
Wipe the hindlimbs of the mice with ethanol wipes.
Inject 10 μL (10 μg/mL) of NTX diluted in PBS intramuscularly into the tibialis anterior muscle at one site per muscle (10 μL per muscle).
Ensure the needle for injection pokes through the fascia but stays at the top of the muscle.
Insert the needle at approximately 45° for injury induction.
Allow mice to recover post-injury depending on the desired time frame after injury.
Euthanize Pax7EGFP mice according to IACUC guidelines.
Collect tibialis anterior (TA) muscle from uninjured and injured Pax7EGFP mice.
Position the mouse spine on a Styrofoam dissection board.
Secure limbs with a 21G needle.
Spray the mouse with 70% ethanol.
Use forceps to pinch and cut an opening horizontally in the center of the mouse belly skin.
Peel off the leg skin by pulling the opening in opposite directions.
Carefully remove the fascia using sharp forceps to expose the underlying TA muscle.
Run the tip of the forceps underneath the TA muscle to detach it from the tibia.
Cut the distal TA tendon and use a dissection scissor to cut the muscle along its longitudinal line.
Remove TA at its proximal attachment carefully.
Place the muscle in a 6 cm dish containing 4% paraformaldehyde/1× PBS buffer on ice.
Wrap the 6 cm dish containing TA muscles with aluminum foil.
Place the 6 cm dish in an orbital shaker in the cold room at 4°C.
Leave TA samples for 2 hours to fix muscle samples.
Aspirate 4% paraformaldehyde from the 6 cm dish.
Wash muscles with 3 mL of 1× phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) three times.
Preserve muscles in 3 mL of 1× PBS.
Mount fixed muscles on a custom-made polycarbonate chamber and immerse in 1× PBS.
Lower a coverslip from the top to close the chamber.
Cut a piece of filter paper based on the size of the inner square.
Apply Elmer’s rubber cement to the back of the polycarbonate window.
Attach the window to the plus slide of the Superfrost plus microscopy slide to create a polycarbonate chamber.
Place the obtained filter paper inside the chamber to decrease movement of muscle samples relative to the chamber.
Use forceps to place one TA muscle inside the chamber carefully.
Apply Elmer’s rubber cement to the top of the polycarbonate window to glue the coverslip to the window.
Use transfer pipets to fill the polycarbonate chamber with 1× PBS.
Carefully lower the cover glass on top of the window to close the chamber.
Use the sharp tip of the forceps to push gently on top of the cover glass.
Use a Kim Wipe to remove excess mounting media (1× PBS).
Perform two-photon imaging of whole-mount uninjured or injured TA muscle.
Visualize the structure of interest using second harmonics (SHG) and green fluorescent proteins in Pax7EGFP mice.
Move the motorized stage from the preparation area to the imaging area.
Place the chamber containing the muscle sample on the motorized stage.
Adjust the XY position of the microscope motorized platform so that the muscle sample is directly underneath the lens.
Secure the chamber by tightening the screw.
Deposit distilled water on top of the coverslip for the water-immersion lens.
Adjust the height of the lens to find focus.
Turn off room lights.
Turn on wide-field epifluorescence and use the eyepiece to find focus.
Turn off the epifluorescence shutter.
Cover the microscope with a blackout chamber or blackout cloth.
Set the laser wavelength at 910 nm for green fluorophore and SHG.
Set the laser power at 13% initially.
Set the detector gain to 100%.
Increase the laser power slowly if the signal remains low.
Turn on tilescan and z-stack.
Adjust XYZ position to find the field of interest where muscle stem cells are visible below the collagen deposition layer.

Format scan settings as follows: Format 1024 × 1024, Speed 400 Hz, Bidirectional ON, Phase X -33.04, Zoom factor 1.5, Image size 369.05 μm × 369.05 μm, Pixel Size 360.75 μm × 360.75 μm, Line Average 2, Tilescan field size 3 × 4 with advanced statistical stitching.
Set the upper limits of a z-stack below the collagen deposition layer.
Set lower limits of a z-stack before muscle cell signal disappears.
Start z-stack acquisition with a step size of 1 or 1.5 μm.
Note: It typically takes two hours to complete scanning for an image with a z-stack depth of about 100 μm and tilescan field size 3 × 4.
Save the original file in .lif format to a hard drive for further data analysis.
Load acquired optical sections from two-photon microscopy into Fiji software.
Stack acquired optical sections in Fiji to define the muscle stem cell number in the TA muscle.
Count MuSCs and normalize them to the volume stacked.
Analyze minimum 100 MuSCs per image using Simple Neurite Tracer (SNT) plugin for quantifying protrusion length and number.
Measure MuSC circularity, aspect ratio, and orientation ratio using set measurements and angle tool in Fiji.
Define cells as misaligned with myofiber if the angle between cell body and myofiber is greater than 15 degrees.
Calculate the ratio of misaligned cells divided by the total number of cells per cell type.
Mark individual cells for analysis using the "multi-point" function.
Click to show the label on all slices.
Create maximum projection of the image.
Go to Image > Stacks > Z project.
Choose Max intensity.
Save the Max projection as a tiff file.
Load saved number selection by dragging the ROI file to Fiji software.
Manually draw a circle encompassing the cell body of the muscle stem cell to obtain cell area and circularity.
Click Analyze > Measure to get area and circularity results.
Use the angle tool to measure the angle between the cell body and the myofiber.
If the measured angle is larger than 15 degrees, consider the cell as misaligned with the fiber.
Calculate the misalignment ratio by dividing the number of cells misaligned by the total number of cells per cell type.
Download the Neuroanatomy plugin to Fiji software for measurement of protrusion length.
Open the Neuroanatomy plugin and load the numbered tiff file.
Select only the XY view in the user interface.
Move along the Z direction and click at the beginning and end of each protrusion to create a path.
In the Path Manager, tag the path and obtain protrusion by selecting Morphometry > Length.
Export data from the Neuroanatomy plugin for copying into Excel.
Find an area full of muscle fibers and use the rectangle tool to select and crop the region of interest.
Obtain dimensions by selecting Image > Show info > Width, Height, Z-step size.
Calculate the volume of the cuboid image filled with muscle fibers.
Create a maximum projection of the selected volume.
Count the total number of MuSCs in the maximum projection image.
Export data from Fiji software and copy it into Excel.
Normalize MuSC numbers to 1 μm3 volume of muscle fibers.
Analyze data in Excel.
Graph datasets as desired in GraphPad Prism.
Group data as number of cells per volume.
Determine MuSC composition based on the number of protrusions.
Calculate MuSC misalignment ratio.
Measure MuSC protrusion length.
Measure MuSC area.
Calculate MuSC circularity.
